items.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: We met about a year ago. We were both teaching at a music camp on Vashon Island in Washington State.

ctx.x: About a year. We met about a year ago. We were both teaching at a music camp on Vashon Island in Washington State. He was teaching bluegrass banjo and I was teaching guitar and vocals I guess. He’s trying to teach me bluegrass.

Bluegrass, as a matter of fact, Cal Collins played a lot of bluegrass, and there’s quite a few similarities I think in jazz — that a lot of it’s improvised, the feel is somewhat different but the concept is not all that different.

Oh yeah, and it’s funny, any kind of music that you don’t know much about, from a distance you think it all sounds alike. Like all Irish music sounds alike, or all Bluegrass music sounds alike. But then when you get into it, my gosh, it’s not the case at all. We’ve started going to hear live Bluegrass and there’s some great groups that are very exciting. So it’s all in the ear of the beholder.
